item.text: {"text":"Focus only on model_design with a Tier 2 architectural change: add a learned fusion of shallow, intermediate, and final convolutional representations to the existing NextItNet encoder. Reducing dropout to 0.1 lowered validation HR@10 from 0.665 to 0.620, so restore 0.2 and pursue a representation change instead of another regularization adjustment. A plausible limitation is that the final readout cannot directly select intermediate features, which may preserve useful recent-item patterns for short histories; this remains a hypothesis to test. Capture the masked encoder states immediately before the convolutional stack, after its midpoint, and after its final block—depths 0, 4, and 8 with the current configuration. Concatenate these states along the channel dimension and apply one bias-free, kernel-size-1 Conv1d mapping 3H channels back to H before the existing final LayerNorm. Initialize its shallow and intermediate channel slices to zero and its final-depth slice to the identity, so the added component initially reproduces the existing readout while learning whether earlier features improve ranking. This fusion remains strictly causal because it combines only representations at the same sequence position, and it produces one NextItNet representation rather than an ensemble of predictions. Preserve the gated local/dilated blocks, residual scales, padding masks, tied item embeddings, scoring logic, constructor and method interfaces, and all eight constants at the supplied best configuration. Implement the addition inside the existing two classes using only the permitted imports, leaving preprocessing, BPR loss, optimizer execution, training, checkpoint selection, evaluation, and submission entirely to the frozen host. Allocate one candidate within the 44-slot budget and compare its host-selected validation HR@10 against 0.665 under the unchanged protocol, retaining the modification only if validation improves and making no claim about an unavailable test metric."}
